## Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Current margins measure training-pair separation. They cannot establish why broadly related items outrank precise matches. (2) User feedback emphasizes recent, repeated evidence. This motivates separate recency and repetition interventions, without treating either as observed intent. (3) The compatibility view already exposes sequence features and candidate scoring. Architecture-aware perturbation probes can therefore extend diagnosis with limited implementation work.

**Related work.** (1) CETRec distinguishes temporal effects, while sequence-pattern research identifies item-availability confounding. Preserve the item multiset when testing order dependence. (2) Semantically Consistent Contrastive Learning cautions that perturbations can change sequence meaning. Interpret removals as model-dependence tests, not preference-preserving augmentations. (3) Sampling-reliability research establishes candidate dependence of ranking metrics. Keep diagnostic candidates fixed and retain the host’s pinned validation metric for selection.

## Framework and directions

| Direction | Observable evidence | Intervention | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal dependence | Sequence positions | Remove recent events; shuffle older events | Position is not elapsed time |
| Repeated interests | Recurring IDs or lexical neighbors | Remove supporting events | Similarity is not intent |
| Specific usefulness | Explicit title/description attributes | Audit conflicting attributes | Unknown compatibility requires abstention |
| Ranking reliability | Fixed candidate scores | Compare target rank and top-10 overlap | Candidate-dependent evidence |

## Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Paired perturbation diagnosis — 5/8/3.** Positive: connects interpretable interventions to scale-invariant ranking changes. Negative: dependence does not establish usefulness or causality. Builds on CETRec and sampling-reliability findings.
2. **Recent-history residual scorer — 4/7/4.** Add a weighted mean of recent item embeddings to SASRec’s final representation. Positive: inexpensive response to reported stale-history influence. Negative: may amplify incidental recent purchases; temporal sensitivity alone does not guarantee improvement.
3. **Evidence-filtered lexical negatives — 6/7/6.** Mix random negatives with lexical neighbors having explicit attribute conflicts. Positive: targets broad-relatedness errors using available text. Negative: sparse attributes and false negatives constrain coverage; Hard-BPR motivates conservative weighting.

## Selected idea: paired perturbation diagnosis

At 0% progress, first establish whether SASRec actually depends on the evidence implicated by feedback. Extend `DiagnosisProbe` with fixed-candidate target ranks, paired intervention deltas, and recommendation overlap.

For sampled training prefixes, score the next observed item against deterministic unseen negatives. Remove recent events, remove repeated-interest support, and shuffle older context separately. Compare removal effects against repeated equal-size random controls; additionally match coarse position and popularity strata where feasible. Report when matching is impossible.

```text
for prefix, target in training_examples:
    candidates = fixed_candidates(prefix, target)
    baseline = rank(prefix, candidates)
    for intervention in supported_interventions:
        measure target_rank_change and top10_overlap
        compare with matched_control_draws
aggregate paired effects, coverage, and missingness
```

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` and its return schema. Diagnose `view.model` in evaluation mode and restore its prior state. Empty samples return null with counts. These probes prioritize subsequent ablations; only unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10 determines whether a trained change improves selection performance.

idea.description: Extend the compatibility-preserving diagnostic adapter with paired sequence interventions evaluated using fixed-candidate target ranks and top-10 overlap. Separate recency, repeated-interest evidence, and older-context order dependence.
idea.motivation: Existing embedding geometry and raw margins cannot resolve the reported mismatch between broad relatedness and specific recent interests. Early-stage research benefits from inexpensive measurements that distinguish plausible failure mechanisms before allocating substantial training budget.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Use only training prefixes and their loader-provided positive targets for these exploratory probes; do not interpret them as validation performance. Right-align retained nonzero events after removal, and document that removal changes positional encoding as well as available evidence. Shuffle only nonpadding older events while holding the latest event fixed. Define repeated-interest groups using exact item recurrence initially; optional TF-IDF title/description similarity must be labeled a proxy. Construct a deterministic diagnostic candidate set per example containing its target and up to 99 distinct nonpadding catalog items excluding known training-history items and the target. Record actual candidate counts when catalogs are small. Reuse candidates across interventions and controls. Define target rank as one plus the number of strictly higher-scoring candidates, with a documented deterministic item-ID tie break. Report rank change, pairwise win rate, top-10 overlap, intervention size, eligible counts, control variability, and unmatched-control counts. Aggregate examples within user before category summaries. Report null for undefined statistics rather than zeros. Inspect the actual view.model, use no_grad, and restore its original training state in a finally block. Batch and cap examples to limit diagnostic GPU cost. Preserve existing valid probes and remove unsupported metadata-category breakdowns. No architecture or predictor change is required for this diagnostic-only proposal; any later scoring modification must update the predictor writer and checkpoint loading together. Keep DATA_DIR as os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preserve all four dataset routes and seeds, and write diagnostic artifacts beneath the trial directory.
idea.pseudocode:
save model.training; model.eval()
try, under no_grad:
  extract a bounded deterministic sample of valid training prefixes and next-item targets
  for each example:
    construct and cache fixed diagnostic candidates
    baseline = score_with_view(prefix, candidates)
    for recent_removal, repetition_removal, older_context_shuffle:
      if intervention is undefined: record missingness; continue
      changed = apply_intervention(prefix)
      score changed sequence through architecture-compatible view
      record target_rank(changed) - target_rank(baseline)
      record pairwise_win_rate and top10_overlap
      for removal interventions:
        sample repeated equal-size random controls
        match coarse position/popularity strata where feasible
        record targeted effect minus mean control effect and matching coverage
  aggregate within user, then by dataset
  return {'metrics': results, 'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions}
finally:
  model.train(saved_training_state)

originality.positive: Combines distinct temporal and repetition interventions with paired, scale-invariant ranking measurements inside the existing architecture compatibility contract.
originality.negative: Perturbation attribution and fixed-candidate ranking are established techniques; the contribution is their disciplined adaptation to this task.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable way to prioritize recency, denoising, and scoring ablations across all four datasets.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity may reflect positional artifacts or training fit and requires downstream validation before supporting model changes.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses sequence encoding and candidate scoring without retraining or new dependencies for the initial exact-recurrence version.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct prefix extraction, candidate exclusion, intervention controls, and architecture-specific feature selection require careful handling.

related_work.title: CETRec
contributions: The supplied research summary distinguishes absolute and relative temporal order and describes counterfactual tuning.
limitations: Temporal sensitivity does not independently establish recommendation usefulness or causal user preferences.

related_work.title: Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns in Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Compares sequence shuffling approaches and identifies item availability as a possible source of apparent sequential signal.
limitations: A simple shuffle probe does not control all availability effects.

related_work.title: Semantically Consistent Contrastive Learning
contributions: Motivates caution when treating cropping, masking, and reordering as semantics-preserving operations.
limitations: Its augmentation motivation does not validate a particular intervention as a faithful explanation.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies
contributions: Examines the reliability of recommendation evaluation under different sampling strategies.
limitations: Fixed diagnostic candidates improve paired comparability but cannot establish full-catalog quality.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: Addresses false-negative harm associated with hard-negative training.
limitations: Does not establish that lexical similarity or attribute disagreement supplies reliable negative relevance labels.
